title: You are the only contributor to Dana who asks for pieces of silver. Then I don’t know about the next number. Fred Ryan wants space for an article on economics.
html_source:
Eglinton’s assertion that no other contributors want to be paid for their contributions is a little dubious. Coupling that to the observation that Fred Ryan, the other editor of the Dana, wants to write about economics underscores that point.

Stephen will contemplate this in the next passage.

The “pieces of silver” idiom probably evokes the price paid to Judas by the Sanhedrin in order to buy his betrayal of Jesus (see Matthew 27). Stephen has recently mentioned Judas in his quotation of Maeterlinck.

Is Eglinton hinting that a writer seeking payment for his work from a publication is akin to Judas seeking payment to betray Jesus? If so, this is employed, comfortable Eglinton expressing his disdain for poor, struggling Stephen.
